summary: [¶] (b) In terms of the judgment dated 28.8.2024 of the APTEL in _Appeal No. 309/2019 (MPPMCL vs DVC)_ , and as confirmed by the Hon’ble Supreme Court vide its order dated 23.9.2024 in _CA No. 10480/2024 (DVC vs. MPPMCL)_ , had categorically held that all matters which would have a bearing upon tariff for a generating company, including issues such as change in law, force majeure, and other matters impacting tariff directly, constitute tariff disputes within the meaning of Section 79(1) of the Act. It also clarified that disputes relating to termination or breach of contract, which do not impact tariff directly or indirectly, were to be considered non-tariff disputes, which are referable to arbitration. [¶] (f) The escalation mechanism under Schedule 6 is embedded within the tariff structure, and any dispute regarding the manner in which the escalation index is to be applied necessarily impacts the payable tariff. In this regard, the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the _State of Himachal Pradesh & Anr. vs JSW Hydro Energy Ltd. & Ors. (2025 SCC OnLine SC 1460), as relied by the Petitioner, held that the_ interpretation of rules and regulations dealing with tariff determination falls within the exclusive jurisdiction of the regulatory commissions. In the present case, given the direct impact of the escalation mechanism on the computation of tariff, this Commission, under Section 79(1) (b) and (f) of the Act, has the power to adjudicate upon the matter. [¶] (g) The decision of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of _Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Limited vs Green Infra Corporate Wind Private Limited & Ors., [(2025) 478 ITR 617]_ , held that the issue of tariff cannot be a matter left to private negotiation or mutual agreements between parties. Consequently, disputes relating to tariff components and their computation cannot be relegated to arbitration, as doing so would defeat the regulatory scheme of the Act. The dispute is therefore not arbitrable and falls within the exclusive jurisdiction of this Hon’ble Commission under Section 79(1) of the Act. [¶] (d) The Petition has been filed for adjudication by this Commission over the correctness or otherwise of the invoices raised, on the basis of the provisions concerning the computation of tariff. The judgment in the _DVC vs MPPMCL_ case held that all matters which would have a bearing upon the tariff for a generating company would constitute a tariff dispute and fall solely within the jurisdiction of this Commission and are not arbitrable. [para 18] 18. Thereafter, the APTEL _vide_ judgment dated 25.2.2026 in Appeal Nos. 348 of 2025 and Ors. (“Tata Power Judgment”), in light of the law declared in the DVC Judgment, held that the disputes, including those which fall within the ambit of regulatory functions of the Commission, or which impact tariff either directly or indirectly, are non-arbitrable, and, notwithstanding an arbitration agreement in existence and the tests stipulated in Section 8(1) of the A&C Act 1996 being satisfied, [¶] contended that the Petitioner has incorrectly applied the escalation on a semi-annual compounding basis rather than annually. On the other hand, the Petitioner has submitted that its computation methodology is strictly in accordance with the escalation framework notified by the Commission from time to time.
